title: Page one
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood writes page one of the novel. On the desk, in pen, in the display face. The strip shows the desk, the pen, the dog, the lamp. It does not show the page. It will never show the page.

panels.composition: The bedroom, night. The desk lamp. WOOD writing, not drawing — a sheet of lined paper, the pen moving in the display face. BARNABY under the table.

image.prompt: a young man at a desk at night writing on lined paper under a lamp with a small dog beneath the table, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pen. The paper's edge. The first line's shape — blocks. The strip looks away.

image.prompt: close on a pen moving across lined paper, the writing rendered as unreadable blocks, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog's chin coming up onto Wood's slipper. The pen stopping. Starting again.

image.prompt: a small dog resting its chin on a young man's slipper beneath a desk as he writes, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The room from the door. The lamp. The back of Wood's head. The page under his hand, face down now. Page one. The strip stays at the door.

image.prompt: a bedroom seen from its doorway with a lamp lit over a young man's back as he turns a page face down on the desk, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Page one. Face down. The strip never shows the page.
